functions.description: Convert a gas sample volume given in dm3, L, cm3 or m3 into cubic metres.
inputs: the volume of the gas sample with unit (dm3, L, cm3 or m3)
outputs: the volume of the gas sample in cubic metres (m3)

functions.description: Convert a temperature given in degrees Celsius or kelvin into kelvin.
inputs: the temperature of the gas with unit (°C or K)
outputs: the temperature of the gas in kelvin (K)

functions.description: Provide the molar gas constant R in SI units of J K-1 mol-1.
outputs: the molar gas constant R in J K-1 mol-1

functions.description: Compute the pressure in pascals of a perfect gas from pV = nRT given amount, gas constant, kelvin temperature and volume in cubic metres.
inputs: the amount of substance of the gas n with unit (mol)
the molar gas constant R in J K-1 mol-1
the temperature of the gas in kelvin (K)
the volume of the gas sample in cubic metres (m3)
outputs: the perfect gas pressure in pascals (Pa)

functions.description: Convert a pressure in pascals into atmospheres.
inputs: the perfect gas pressure in pascals (Pa)
outputs: the perfect gas pressure in atmospheres (atm)

functions.description: Cross-check a perfect gas pressure in atmospheres by recomputing p = nRT/V with R in L atm K-1 mol-1 and volume in litres, then compare it with the primary result.
inputs: the amount of substance of the gas n with unit (mol)
the temperature of the gas in kelvin (K)
the volume of the gas sample with unit (dm3, L, cm3 or m3)
the perfect gas pressure in atmospheres (atm)
outputs: agreement of the cross-check with the primary pressure

functions.description: Predict the pressure exerted by a perfect gas from its amount, identity, volume and temperature.
inputs: the amount of substance of the gas n with unit (mol)
the chemical identity of the gas as a name or formula with state (gas phase)
the volume of the gas sample with unit (dm3, L, cm3 or m3)
the temperature of the gas with unit (°C or K)
outputs: the predicted pressure of the perfect gas in atmospheres (atm)
the predicted pressure of the perfect gas in pascals (Pa)

entry_points.text: Suppose that ●1 of ●2 is confined to ●3 at ●4. Predict the pressure exerted by the ●2 from the perfect gas.

params.description: the amount of substance of the gas n with unit (mol)
params.validity_range: Strictly positive real number (n > 0) in moles; a zero or negative amount has no physical pressure, and very large amounts are valid only while the perfect gas approximation holds.

params.description: the chemical identity of the gas as a name or formula with state (gas phase)
params.validity_range: Any substance that can be treated as a perfect gas at the given conditions; the perfect gas model is most accurate for light, weakly interacting gases far from condensation, and the identity does not otherwise enter the ideal gas calculation.

params.description: the volume of the gas sample with unit (dm3, L, cm3 or m3)
params.validity_range: Strictly positive volume (V > 0) with a unit convertible to m3 or L; a zero volume would give an unbounded pressure, so the value must be positive and physically meaningful for the sample.

params.description: the temperature of the gas with unit (°C or K)
params.validity_range: Temperature must be above absolute zero, i.e. greater than -273.15 °C or greater than 0 K; the result is only physically meaningful for temperatures where the gas remains gaseous and behaves as a perfect gas.

entry_points.text: Suppose that 10.0 mol C2H6(g) is confined to 4.860 dm3 at 27°C. Predict the pressure exerted by the ethane from the perfect gas.
